time.desc: Netizens have successively submitted reports to higher education institutions on the conduct and academic integrity of the accusers.
Some netizens have submitted reporting materials on their conduct to the institution where the accuser intends to study.
The family of the accused party filed a civil lawsuit with the court, requesting the university to revoke the punishment, restore its reputation and compensate

The person in charge of the university involved responded that it was being dealt with and needed to wait for arrangements from superiors. Public opinion demanded that the accuser's relevant qualifications be revoked.
The university involved issued a notice to set up a special working group to launch an investigation and review of the penalties and the papers involved.
Police officers came to warn the short video blogger who accused Fang of plagiarizing his master's thesis and asked him to stop publishing relevant videos.
A blogger revealed that the accuser’s attorney has long been dedicated to LGBT-related legal services and has represented many gender-related cases.

The accused party reported to the relevant agencies that there were obvious discrepancies between the statement of the plaintiff in the judgment and the actual recording evidence, and requested the initiation of liability proceedings citing regulations.
A graduate student reported with his real name that the master's thesis contained many flaws and was suspected of being written by AI. The crackdown on counterfeiting continues to rage.

The graduate student who reported the thesis was asked by four police officers to stop following up. A man at the scene left controversial remarks. The school later clarified that the man was not a member of the school or ordered by the school.
The graduate student who reported the thesis issued a statement that he would stop following up after the police came to his door.

Some scholars have published an article criticizing the characterization of "false accusation cases" and saying that the judgment was improperly reasoned. They believe that the fundamental crux is that the local law's definition of "sexual harassment" may be too narrow.
An alumnus of the university involved and a researcher at a research institution publicly condemned the incident and called for the harshest punishment to be imposed on the accuser.
Another relevant person formally filed a lawsuit against the university involved, demanding a public apology from the school. The incident entered legal proceedings for the first time.
The admissions school clarified the accuser's application, saying it had never accepted his application and that previous rumors were untrue.
After losing the first instance, the accuser was accused of continuing to incite online violence and threatening and harassing the presiding judge.
A blogger exposed the issue of transcript fraud during the qualification examination process of the accuser, and his previous award-winning paper was also accused of academic integrity issues.
The verdict circulated online was found to have been artificially deleted with key evidence records, raising questions about the manipulation of public opinion.

During the defense of the accused party's rights, several andrology experts concluded through video identification that his scratching movements were consistent with the characteristics of related skin diseases.
The accused party submitted dermatological medical records for many years during the defense of his rights, confirming that he had long suffered from related skin diseases.

Posts appeared on the content platform alleging that an account was systematically "clearing ground" for the accuser and discrediting the accused. It was suspected that there was a professional public opinion manipulation team.
The losing party in the first instance filed an appeal and was formally accepted by the second instance court, and the case entered the second instance procedure.
Mainstream media published comments criticizing the university involved for delaying corrections even after the verdict, citing waiting for superiors.

It was revealed that the university involved hid the disciplinary documents on the school network, with only the school IP visible. This was interpreted as a wait-and-see strategy awaiting the final judicial review.

Several insiders from the accused party’s high school alma mater showed their identity certificates to reporters and confirmed that they had a history of misconduct in high school. Relevant revelations have been repeatedly deleted and banned from social platforms.

The court made a ruling on a controversial case of sexual harassment in a university library and determined that the behavior of the boy involved did not constitute sexual harassment. The woman said she would continue to report it
The dissertation involved was removed from mainstream academic literature platforms, and the platform stated that retraction required procedures such as a retraction letter from the university.

The court made a second-instance ruling on a dispute over a university library and upheld the main points of the first-instance, confirming that the accused did not constitute sexual harassment and the case entered judicial finality.

There was a personnel change at the top level of the university involved. The original party committee secretary no longer held the position and was replaced by someone else. The day after the new secretary took office, the school issued a notice revoking the punishment.

It is revealed that the accuser expressed to his attorney that he was on the verge of collapse long before public opinion broke out on a large scale, requesting a verdict as soon as possible, and "it is okay to lose the case."

After the final judicial review upheld the original verdict, the demerit penalty imposed on the accused was revoked, many relevant personnel from the university involved were held accountable, and the accuser's master's degree was still found to be qualified.

The university issued a situation notice: the disciplinary action against the punished students was revoked, the relevant management and tutors were dealt with, and the graduate thesis involved was concluded as "not academic misconduct but with a large number of irregularities" and the degree was maintained.

The universities involved announced the accountability situation in the notification, including suspending the relevant tutors' enrollment qualifications for two years and giving intra-party warnings or admonitions to managers.
The university involved clarified in the report that the rumor that "accused Uncle Fang of holding the title A within the school" was untrue.
The university involved issued a refutation statement after the final handling report, focusing on clarifying many online rumors.
Organization K issued a notice canceling the demerit penalty against Person A, maintaining Person B's master's degree, and launching accountability for the relevant responsible persons.

Institution K formed an expert investigation team to review and formally revoked the sanction of Person A. It determined that Person B’s master’s thesis was not plagiarized and the degree would not be revoked.

The disclosure review of the university involved was completed by an investigation team composed of five experts. A total of 21 people were investigated, 91 pieces of information and evidence were reviewed, and it was finally determined that there was no plagiarism problem in the paper.
